costGuide.title: Mercedes-Benz OM628 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an OM628 engine typically takes 15-20 hours at £75-£95/hr (independent specialist) - the engine bay is incredibly tight, often requiring a subframe drop or engine-out approach via the top.
paragraphs: What genuinely moves the price for this engine is whether the notoriously difficult rear-mounted timing chain has been replaced, and the condition of the bi-turbo oil feed lines. Because the OM628 is a highly complex V8, recon specialists will typically strip the entire top end to clean carbon buildup and replace all turbo oil lines as standard. For a full breakdown of market rates, see our full reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: Mercedes-Benz OM628 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Rear-Mounted Timing Chain Wear - All variants
items.whatHappens: Unlike most engines, the OM628’s timing chains and tensioners are located at the rear of the engine (gearbox end). Over time, the chains stretch and the plastic guides shatter, causing a distinct metallic rattle on cold starts. If ignored, the engine will jump time and destroy the valves and pistons.
items.repairVsReplace: Because of the rear placement, replacing the timing chain requires complete engine removal and disassembly. If the chain has already skipped or damaged the head, a full reconditioned or rebuilt OM628 engine is the only financially viable path.

items.title: Turbocharger Oil Feed Coking - Bi-turbo setup
items.whatHappens: The twin Garrett turbochargers rely on specific oil feed lines that are prone to heat-soak and coking, especially if oil change intervals were extended. Restricted oil flow starves the turbo bearings, leading to shaft play, severe whining, blue smoke, and eventual catastrophic turbo failure.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught before the turbos destroy themselves, the oil feed lines and banjo bolts can be replaced. If the turbos have failed and sent metal through the engine, a full replacement unit is required.

items.title: Injector Seal Weeping & Intake Carbon Buildup - All variants
items.whatHappens: The complex intake manifold houses swirl flaps that become clogged with EGR soot, restricting airflow and triggering limp mode. Simultaneously, the copper injector seals degrade, leading to "Black Death" (hardened carbon rock around the injectors) which can make injector removal nearly impossible without damaging the cylinder head.
items.repairVsReplace: Intake manifolds often require replacement or professional ultrasonic cleaning. Injector seal replacement is mandatory preventative maintenance on any OM628.

failures.goodYearsLine: The OM628 is an incredibly strong but highly complex engine. Units with meticulously documented timing chain and turbo oil line maintenance are highly prized, but neglected examples can easily generate repair bills that exceed the host vehicle's entire market value .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Mercedes-Benz OM628
variants.intro: ═══════════════════════════════════════ The engine code is stamped on the left-hand side of the cylinder block, near the bellhousing. It will also be listed on your V5C logbook under "Engine Capacity" or visible via a VIN decode. The OM628 is sometimes confused with its direct successor, the OM629 (which introduced piezo injectors and different emissions hardware), or the petrol M113 V8 which shares the same engine bay footprint in the W220. Fitting the wrong revision or assuming interchangeability matters significantly: the OM628 requires a specific ECU, transmission torque converter mapping, and bi-turbo exhaust plumbing that will not function correctly if swapped with a petrol V8 or the later OM629 CDI.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement OM628 Engine - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used OM628 engine is an extreme financial risk unless it comes with verifiable, recent documentation of a rear timing chain replacement and turbo oil feed line upgrades. Given the engine-out labour required to fix these items, buying a used unit with unknown history often leads to an immediate £3,000+ teardown bill.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned OM628 engine is the only sensible choice for most buyers. A reputable rebuild will proactively address the fatal flaws by installing new rear timing chains, tensioners, and upgraded turbo oil feed lines, while ultrasonically cleaning the complex intake manifold.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full OM628 engine rebuild is justified for pristine W463 G-Class restorations or low-mileage W211 E-Class examples where maximum longevity and originality are required. An upgraded rebuild should include line-boring, balanced internals, and upgraded turbo coolant and oil lines.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your OM628 engine is installed by specialists equipped for heavy V8 diesel extraction, backed by a nationwide warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The OM628 is typically found in vehicles valued between £2,500 and £8,000 for standard W220 and W163 examples, though low-mileage W211 and W463 models command higher premiums. Because a full OM628 replacement can easily total a standard W220 S-Class, evaluate the vehicle's scrap or parts value before committing to the repair .

items.question: What is the most common failure on the OM628 engine?
items.answer: The most documented and costly issues are rear-mounted timing chain wear, turbocharger oil feed line coking, and injector seal weeping. The rear timing chain location requires complete engine removal for access, making preventative maintenance critical, while coked oil lines can starve the twin turbos and cause catastrophic bearing failure. → Get quotes for a rebuilt OM628 with these issues resolved

items.question: Which Mercedes models use the OM628 engine?
items.answer: The OM628 was fitted to the W220 S-Class (S 400 CDI), the W211 E-Class (E 400 CDI), the W463 G-Class (G 400 CDI), and the W163 M-Class (ML 400 CDI), serving as Mercedes' first V8 diesel for their heaviest and most luxurious chassis between 2000 and 2005. → Check your registration to confirm your exact OM628 fitment

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned OM628 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned OM628 is strongly recommended over a used unit. A proper rebuild will proactively address the fatal flaws by installing new rear timing chains, tensioners, and upgraded turbo oil feed lines, whereas a used engine with unknown history often leads to an immediate £3,000+ teardown bill if the chains or turbos fail shortly after installation. → Compare reconditioned OM628 engine prices from UK specialists
